processing: A flat, straight green tea of buds and young leaf: heated to stop oxidation, pressed flat, and dried until smooth and glossy.
harvest_season: Picked before Qingming. First grade is one bud with a just-opening leaf, the bud longer than the leaf; lower grades take a little more leaf.
appearance_dry: Elegant, flat, straight buds, even and glossy green.
appearance_wet: Tender, even, bright green buds and leaves.
taste_profile: Fresh, clean and brisk, with a lasting light aroma and a smooth finish.

brewing.notes: Bud-heavy grades do best at about 80°C. Raise it a few degrees for lower grades with more leaf.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's pre-Qingming harvest, in three grades defined by the ratio of bud to leaf. Like other greens it is best within about a year of picking.
description:
Hongya green tea comes from Hongya County in Meishan, on the southwest rim of the Sichuan basin, in the country around Wawu Mountain. It is a flat, straight, bud-forward green, one of the many neat modern Sichuan teas made to be picked early.

The appellation defines the tea largely by what is picked. Harvest happens before Qingming, and grades run from a bud with a barely opening leaf down to one bud with up to two opening leaves. Cultivars include Mingshan 131, Mingshan 311 and Fuding Dabai.

The cup is bright yellow-green, fresh and clean, without heavy body. Think of it as a light morning tea, and keep the water near 80°C so that the delicate aroma stays intact.

The protected zone covers 15 townships, and the county also promotes organic production, so organic-labelled lots are a realistic find. The grade tells you most: look at how much bud is in the bag and whether the picking date is this spring.
history:
Local writing traces tea drinking in Hongya back to the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, by inference from old texts that mention tea in Sichuan generally. That is a broad regional claim, not a record of this tea.

The documented story is recent. The county has barred heavily polluting industry since 1999 and built an organic tea base, and the name was registered as an agricultural geographical indication on 20 December 2011.
